1zrpw4pjgvm: ## Deploying an agent means giving it rights
1clf6ks3996: Until now, everything ran on fictional data. A real deployment gives the agent an **identity**, **access**, a **budget** and **users**. Each is a risk surface. This course's rule stays: **nothing is deployed without the agreement of the account and environment owner**, and each step is prepared to be simple, repeatable and reversible.
4qg3rbvacb: - **Lab**: fictional or synthetic data, test subscription or tenant, capped costs, destroyed without regret.
1dmf513v3hm: - **Pre-production**: representative but minimized data, same controls as production, used for shadow mode (module 17).
kix5lq2fi6: - **Production**: minimal rights, approvals, logs, named owner.
1c46v4fqpaf: Each environment has **its own identities and secrets**. A lab key that works in production is an architecture flaw.
fgnql6z6sp: Microsoft documentation explains that a **managed identity** lets a component hosted in Azure obtain a Microsoft Entra token **without managing a secret**: the credentials are not even accessible to developers, and there is no additional cost for the identity itself. There are two types: **system-assigned** (tied to the resource lifecycle) and **user-assigned** (standalone, reusable resource). When a service does not support Entra authentication, you store its credentials in **Azure Key Vault** and access them with the managed identity.
16z7i101ros: - No secret in code, repository, instructions, logs or plain-text variables.
140833e6rd2: - One identity per agent, with **minimal roles** on the targeted resources (log reading, no administration rights).
2b7thnhf4p0: - Documented rotation and revocation; short token lifetime.
1cc44hzkns0: - A secret discovered in a repository is **considered compromised**: revoke it, even if the repository is private.
k28oq1jwax: A manual deployment in a portal is neither repeatable nor reviewable. Describe resources in versioned templates (Bicep, ARM, Terraform): peer review, history, identical recreation, **clean destruction**. For this course, the "deployment recipes" are instructions and templates to read and adapt; nothing is deployed in your account unless you decide so.
12sgjzj5u4l: Repository, tests (module 17), secret scanning, configuration validation, then deployment to pre-production, approval, then production. Steps that touch production require **human approval** in the pipeline. The pipeline's secrets are protected variables, never values from the repository.

pgevcyusxg: ## The agent is a system in operation
1e4f242yjos: A deployed agent behaves like any service: it fails, drifts, costs, gets attacked and must be maintained. If nobody answers for it, it will become a risk. The NIST AI risk management framework insists on governance and monitoring throughout the lifecycle.
e141fmwde1: - **Owner**: answers for the agent, its results and its risks; decides on withdrawal.
21p9mqbb71h: Name the people and their backups. An agent whose owner has left is an orphan agent: reassign or retire.
25s1b3i2m0b: A document (maintained as in module 15) that answers: what the agent is for and what its limits are; how to know it is doing well (dashboard, thresholds); what to do if the refusal rate explodes, if the cost drifts, if the model is unavailable; how to activate the emergency switch; how to roll back; who to notify; how to rotate secrets; how to make a change. Each section names **who** can do **what**.
2afi2i1kcuf: Analysts must know what the agent does **well**, **badly** and **never**: it proposes, they decide; a cited evidence is verified; an instruction in data is reported; "no indicator" is not "benign". Without this training, automation bias (module 17) sets in.
28hm5hiwb60: Quarterly: evaluation set replayed, rights review, cost review, incident review, runbook review, verification that approvals are still read. Each review produces recorded decisions: maintain, fix, reduce powers or retire.
syolrkjlyp: An agent incident is handled like any other (module 16) and feeds a report (module 15) with lessons, owners and deadlines. Each incident adds a case to the test set.
16uleuluc6: Retiring an agent is a management act, not an oversight: disabling tools, revoking the identity and secrets, archiving logs per policy, deleting resources, informing users, updating the inventory. Retirement criteria: thresholds not met, unjustified cost, absent owner, replacement by a better solution, unacceptable risk.
